ov: Seven species of ocean-going turtles, including the green, loggerhead, hawksbill and leatherback. Five of the seven are threatened with extinction. Unlike many turtles, they can’t pull their head and flippers into the shell, but the streamlined shape helps them swim.

why.et: Long eaten as a delicacy, such as turtle soup in 1700s England, and still harvested for food in many places.

rg: Oceans worldwide; females come ashore only to lay eggs.
df: Varies by species: crabs, sponges, molluscs, jellyfish and their relatives, worms, fish, seagrass and seaweed. Adult green turtles eat only plants.
fx: Sea turtles navigate using the Earth’s magnetic field.
Nesting females come ashore almost always at night and dig a nest 40–50 cm deep with their hind flippers.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is mostly confirmed: some females return to the beach where they hatched. The "30 years later" figure isn’t in the article. Suggested wording: "Some females return to the very beach where they hatched to lay their eggs." No why.et: the source doesn’t cover eating turtles.
